The test image shows a soybean plant with **green stems remaining** while the surrounding field is completely matured/senesced (dry, brown). Some leaves are still green on the plant while surrounding plants are fully dry. This strongly suggests **Green_stem_disorder** or possibly **Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus** (which can also cause green stems).

Let me view reference images to confirm.

The Green_stem_disorder reference matches very well — green stems persisting with mature/dry pods nearby, just like the test image. Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus shows mosaic mottling patterns not present in the test image.

Let me check a few more to ensure no confusion with other diseases.

Neither Soybean_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus (dark, wrinkled, small leaves) nor Sudden_death_syndrome (interveinal chlorosis/necrosis) match the test image.

The test image is a clear case of **Green_stem_disorder**: a single soybean plant with green, moist stems and some green leaves while the entire surrounding field has fully senesced and is dry/brown. No lesions, no mottling, no chlorosis patterns — just the classic "green island" in a mature field.
